shots.phrase: Begin by framing Pipeline Overview as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: A vertex shader modifies position and color attributes for each triangle vertex before they reach the rasterizer.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Primitive Assembly precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Three connected vertices form a triangle primitive that the rasterizer will convert into a set of pixel candidates.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Clipping Process operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: A large triangle extending beyond the camera's field of view is clipped to fit within the viewport boundaries.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Rasterization Conversion and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: Each pixel within the clipped triangle receives a set of interpolated vertex attributes for processing.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Interpolation Mechanism to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: Color and texture coordinates are calculated for each pixel based on the weighted average of the triangle's vertex attributes.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Fragment Processing, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: A fragment shader applies a lighting model to each pixel, calculating final color based on material properties and light direction.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Depth Testing & Visibility with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Consider this worked case: A closer triangle overwrites a farther triangle's pixels because its depth values are smaller than the stored depth buffer.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Blending Operations to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Consider this worked case: A semi-transparent overlay triangle mixes its computed color with the background color using a specified alpha factor.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Coordinate Spaces & Projections to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Vertices are transformed from model space to clip space using a projection matrix before being converted to normalized device coordinates.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
On screen, list a checklist with checkboxes for: 1.
Depth and blending parameter validation.
